UR-A01.text: Block suspended users from signing in immediately, and log every account creation, suspension, or restoration.
acceptance: An administrator can create a new user account, suspend an active account, or restore a suspended account from the Admin Users screen.
A suspended user is immediately blocked from signing in or using protected pages until restored.
Every account creation, suspension, or restoration is saved in the activity log with the admin's name, reason, and time.

UR-A02.text: Require a written reason whenever an admin rejects, suspends, or asks for corrections on a listing, and send it to the owner.
acceptance: An administrator can open any submitted listing in the approval queue and choose Approve, Reject, Request Corrections, Suspend, or Restore.
Rejecting, suspending, or asking for corrections requires the administrator to write a clear reason for the property owner.
The property owner receives an automatic notification whenever their listing status changes.

UR-A07.text: Give administrators a screen to search and filter the activity log by user, action, or date.
acceptance: An administrator can view and filter the activity log by person, action type, record, or date.
Activity log entries are permanent and cannot be edited or deleted by anyone.

UR-A08.text: Log the old value, new value, admin name, and time whenever a platform setting is changed.
acceptance: An administrator can view and update platform-wide settings and feature switches from the Admin Settings screen.
Every change to a setting records the old value, the new value, who changed it, and when.

UR-AN01.text: Lock all administrator screens and actions so only signed-in administrators can open them.
acceptance: Only signed-in administrators can open admin pages or run admin actions.
Guests, property owners, and property staff are automatically blocked if they try to open any admin link.

UR-AN02.text: Make activity log records permanent so no one can edit or delete past entries.
acceptance: Every important action (approvals, rejections, role changes, suspensions, setting updates) automatically creates a permanent log entry.
The database blocks any attempt to alter or erase past log entries.

UR-G01.text: Provide a complete sign-up, confirmation, sign-in, and sign-out flow for all users.
acceptance: A new user can create an account with their email and password, confirm their email code/link, and sign in.
A signed-in user can sign out at any time or reset a forgotten password through their confirmed email.

UR-O01.text: Give property owners a step-by-step verification form and a live status tracker (Pending, Needs Correction, Approved, Rejected).
acceptance: A property owner can complete onboarding by uploading their Ghana Card, proof of property ownership/authorisation, and Ghana Tourism Authority (GTA) licence.
The owner can check their verification status at any time (Pending Review, Needs Correction, Approved, or Rejected) and see reviewer notes.

UR-O02.text: Let verified owners manage all parts of their listings and room availability from the Owner Portal.
acceptance: Once verified, an owner can create, edit, pause, and manage property listings—including rooms/units, photos, nightly prices in GHS, amenities, house rules, and available dates.
Owners who have not yet been verified cannot submit or publish a listing.

UR-O03.text: Provide a simple calendar screen for each room where owners or staff can click to block or open dates.
acceptance: An owner or authorised staff member can view a calendar for each room/unit and block or unblock dates when the unit is unavailable.
The system prevents two unavailable blocks from overlapping on the same unit for the same dates.

UR-O15.text: Let property owners invite staff members to their company and manage what each staff member can do.
acceptance: An owner can invite staff members to their organisation and choose which properties and actions each staff member is allowed to manage.
An owner can remove a staff member's access to a property at any time, and the change takes effect immediately.

UR-ON01.text: Keep screens clean and simple so small guesthouse and hotel owners can use FindStay without training.
acceptance: Screens use clear headings, everyday language, and step-by-step forms so small property owners can use FindStay without training.
Key tasks like uploading verification documents, adding a property, or blocking dates take only a few clear steps.

UR-ON02.text: Show each property owner only their own company’s properties, documents, and records.
acceptance: Each property owner and their staff can see and manage only their own organisation's properties, units, documents, and records.
One owner can never view or edit another owner's properties or documents.

UR-ON05.text: Keep the live website running reliably with daily backups so property owners never lose their records.
acceptance: The database is backed up automatically every day, and the team tests restoring a backup to prove no records will be lost.
Automatic health checks alert the team if the website or server goes down.

UR-PM03.text: Let owners assign specific tasks (such as editing a listing or blocking calendar dates) to each staff member.
acceptance: An owner or manager can assign specific permissions (such as viewing a listing, editing details, or managing the calendar) to each staff member.
Every permission grant or removal is saved and logged.

UR-PS01.text: Show property staff only the specific properties and tools they have been given permission to use.
acceptance: A property staff member only sees the specific properties and tools that the owner has given them permission to use.
If a staff member tries to open or edit another property in the same company without permission, the system blocks the request.

UR-PSN01.text: Hide sensitive owner identity documents (such as Ghana Card details) from property staff accounts.
acceptance: Property staff cannot view sensitive owner identity documents (like Ghana Card numbers) or change company-wide staff roles.
Each staff account is restricted to only the tasks required for their job.

FR-01.text: Let guests, property owners, property staff, and administrators create or receive accounts for their role.
acceptance: People can create or receive accounts for their role (Guest, Property Owner/Manager, Property Staff, or Administrator).
A single account can hold role memberships (for example, being a Guest while also managing or working at a property) without needing separate email addresses.

FR-02.text: Check that a user is signed in before opening any private page or running any private server action.
acceptance: Every private page and action checks that the user is signed in with a valid session before allowing access.
Anyone who is not signed in is redirected to the sign-in screen.

FR-03.text: Let users sign in with their email and password and sign out from any device.
acceptance: A registered user can sign in with their email and password and stay signed in safely while using the app.
Clicking Sign Out ends the session immediately so the account cannot be used from that browser without signing in again.

FR-04.text: Let users reset a forgotten password through a single-use link sent to their confirmed email.
acceptance: A user who forgets their password can request a password reset link sent to their confirmed email address.
The reset link expires after a short time and can only be used once to set a new password.

FR-05.text: Send a confirmation code or link by email (or phone OTP) to verify new accounts.
acceptance: New accounts must confirm their email address (or phone code when SMS is enabled) before they are treated as verified.
Incorrect or expired confirmation codes are rejected with a clear message telling the user how to request a new code.

FR-06.text: Let signed-in users view and update their own profile details (full name, phone number, photo, and language).
acceptance: A signed-in user can view and update their own name, phone number, profile photo, and language preference.
A user cannot edit another person's profile or change their own approval status.

FR-07.text: Check the signed-in user’s role and permissions before showing any screen or allowing any server action.
acceptance: Every screen and server action checks the user's role and permissions before showing data or saving changes.
Users who do not have permission for an action receive a clear 'Access denied' message.

FR-08.text: Let property owners submit their Ghana Card, property ownership proof, and tourism licence for admin review, and resubmit if corrections are needed.
acceptance: A property owner can submit their Ghana Card details, proof of property ownership/authorisation, and Ghana Tourism Authority licence for admin review.
If an administrator asks for corrections, the owner can upload updated documents and send the application back for review.

FR-09.text: Let property owners and administrators grant or remove specific property permissions for staff members.
acceptance: Owners and administrators can grant or remove specific property permissions for staff members.
Permission changes take effect right away without requiring the staff member to create a new account.

FR-11.text: Let verified property owners create a new property listing in draft mode.
acceptance: A verified property owner can create a new property listing in draft mode and fill in its details step by step.
An owner whose verification has not yet been approved is prompted to complete verification before creating or submitting a listing.

FR-12.text: Let owners and authorised staff edit an existing listing’s details, rooms, photos, prices, amenities, and rules.
acceptance: An owner or authorised staff member can update an existing listing's title, description, location, rooms/units, photos, prices, amenities, and house rules.
Saved updates are validated so required information cannot be accidentally erased.

FR-13.text: Let owners pause or deactivate a published listing whenever they want to hide it from search.
acceptance: An owner can pause or deactivate a published listing whenever they want to stop showing it to guests.
A paused listing is hidden from public search until the owner resumes it.

FR-14.text: Let owners upload property and room photos, reorder them, and pick a main cover photo.
acceptance: An owner can upload photos for their property and rooms, reorder them, and choose a cover photo.
Only valid image files within the size limit are accepted, and uploaded photos are optimised for fast loading.

FR-15.text: Let owners set the property type and add individual rooms/units with guest capacity, bedrooms, and bathrooms.
acceptance: An owner can set the property's accommodation type (Hotel, Budget Hotel, Guesthouse, or Serviced Apartment) and add individual bookable units/rooms with guest capacity, bedrooms, and bathrooms.
Each unit is tracked individually so its calendar cannot be double-booked, and similar units can be grouped by category for display.

FR-16.text: Let owners tick available amenities (Wi-Fi, AC, generator, parking, etc.) and write house rules.
acceptance: An owner can select available amenities (such as Wi-Fi, Air Conditioning, Backup Generator, Water Tank, Parking, Security) and write clear house rules (check-in/out times, smoking, pets).
Selected amenities and house rules are saved with the listing and shown on the listing preview.

FR-17.text: Let owners set the nightly price in Ghana Cedis (GHS) for each room or unit.
acceptance: An owner can set the nightly price in Ghana Cedis (GHS) for each unit or room category.
Prices are saved accurately in integer pesewas so there are never rounding errors.

FR-18.text: Let owners and authorised staff block or unblock unavailable date ranges on any room’s calendar.
acceptance: An owner or authorised staff member can mark specific date ranges as unavailable on any unit's calendar and remove those blocks when dates open up.
End dates must be after start dates, and changes appear on the unit calendar right away.

FR-21.text: Publish a listing only after both the owner is verified and an administrator approves the listing.
acceptance: A listing goes live (Published) only after both the owner's verification is Approved and an administrator approves the submitted listing.
An owner cannot publish their own listing directly without administrator approval.

FR-22.text: Check that all required fields and photos are complete before allowing a listing to be submitted for approval.
acceptance: Before a listing can be submitted for approval, the system checks that all required details are complete: title, description, Takoradi area, accommodation type, at least 1 unit with capacity, nightly price, at least 3 photos, amenities, and house rules.
If anything is missing, the system highlights the exact missing items so the owner can fill them in.

FR-39.text: Show a live availability calendar for each room and block overlapping unavailable dates.
acceptance: Each unit has a real-time availability calendar showing which dates are open and which dates are blocked.
If two people try to block overlapping dates for the same unit at the same time, the database saves the first one and blocks the duplicate.

FR-68.text: Send an automatic alert to the property owner whenever their verification or listing status changes.
acceptance: Whenever an owner's verification status or listing approval status changes, the owner is notified automatically with the decision and any reviewer notes.
The notification appears both in the app and by email (and SMS when enabled).

FR-69.text: Send formatted email notifications for account, verification, and listing updates.
acceptance: Important account, verification, and listing updates are sent to the user's confirmed email address using clear, readable templates.
If an email fails to send, the system records the failure and retries automatically.

FR-70.text: Support sending SMS alerts to Ghana phone numbers (+233), falling back to email when SMS is switched off.
acceptance: The notification system supports sending SMS alerts to Ghana phone numbers (+233) through a local SMS provider.
If SMS is switched off during initial testing, the system falls back to email notifications without interrupting the user.

FR-71.text: Notify users in the app and by email when they receive a staff invite, permission change, or account update.
acceptance: Users receive notifications for important account events such as staff invitations, permission updates, and account status changes.
Users can see their recent notifications inside the portal and mark them as read.

FR-86.text: Give administrators a summary dashboard showing counts of pending verifications, pending listings, live listings, and users.
acceptance: Administrators have a dedicated dashboard showing counts of pending owner verifications, listings waiting for approval, published listings, and recent activity.
Clicking any summary card takes the administrator straight to that queue.

FR-87.text: Let administrators search user accounts, create new accounts, suspend accounts, and restore suspended accounts.
acceptance: Administrators can search user accounts, create new accounts, suspend accounts that break rules, and restore suspended accounts.
Every user management action requires a reason and is recorded in the activity log.

FR-88.text: Let administrators Approve, Reject, Request Corrections, Suspend, or Restore any submitted listing.
acceptance: Administrators can review submitted listings and Approve, Reject, Request Corrections, Suspend, or Restore them.
Every listing decision saves a status history record, logs the administrator's reason, and notifies the property owner.

FR-92.text: Let administrators view and update platform settings and feature on/off switches from a settings screen.
acceptance: Administrators can view and update platform settings and feature on/off switches from a settings screen without needing code changes.
Only administrators can view internal switches or save setting changes.

NFR-01.text: Guide users through tasks step-by-step with uncluttered screens that need no manual.
acceptance: Screens are clean and uncluttered, guiding owners and admins through each task step by step.
New pilot owners can register, submit verification documents, and create a listing without needing a manual.

NFR-02.text: Use clear, plain-English labels on all menus, buttons, and form inputs (with examples like +233 or GHS).
acceptance: Menus, buttons, and form fields use plain, consistent labels across all pages.
Input fields include helpful examples (such as phone format +233 or prices in GHS) so users know what to enter.

NFR-03.text: Show a loading spinner while saving and a clear success or error banner after every button click.
acceptance: Every button click or form submission shows a clear loading indicator followed by a visible confirmation or error message.
If a form has an error, the message explains clearly how to fix it right next to the field.

NFR-04.text: Connect every form input to a label and make sure all buttons and popups work with a keyboard (Tab, Enter, Escape).
acceptance: All forms, buttons, menus, and popups work with a keyboard (Tab, Enter, Escape) and screen readers.
Every input field has a properly connected label and clear focus outline.

NFR-05.text: Pair every navigation icon and status badge with a readable text label—never show an icon by itself.
acceptance: Main navigation links, property types, amenities, and status badges pair a clear icon with a text label.
Icons never appear alone without a readable label.

NFR-07.text: Use high-contrast text and show both an icon and words on status badges (not just red/green colour).
acceptance: Status badges (Approved, Pending, Needs Correction, Rejected) use icons and text labels—never colour alone—so people with colour-vision differences can read them easily.
Text and button colours have strong contrast against the background.

NFR-09.text: Make all Owner and Admin screens fit mobile phones (360px wide), tablets, and desktop computers.
acceptance: All Owner and Admin screens adjust smoothly to fit small mobile phones (360px wide), tablets, and desktop screens.
Buttons and tap targets on mobile are large enough to tap comfortably without mis-clicking.

NFR-10.text: Test all screens on Chrome, Edge, Firefox, and Safari.
acceptance: The website works properly in current versions of Chrome, Edge, Firefox, and Safari on both phone and desktop.
Pages open without visual glitches or broken buttons across all four browsers.

NFR-12.text: Prevent sideways (horizontal) scrolling on mobile phone screens.
acceptance: On mobile phones (360px width), pages fit the screen width cleanly without sideways scrolling.
Tables or wide lists either stack neatly into mobile cards or scroll inside their own container.

NFR-17.text: Reject files over 5 MB or invalid file types before upload, and optimise photos so pages load fast on mobile data.
acceptance: Uploaded listing photos are automatically compressed and converted into lightweight WebP images so pages load fast and use less mobile data.
Oversized files (over 5 MB) or non-image files are blocked before upload with a friendly message.

NFR-19.text: Reject any request to a private server route if the sign-in pass is missing or expired.
acceptance: All private screens and server routes require a valid sign-in session before returning any data.
Unsigned visitors cannot view or change any owner, staff, or admin records.

NFR-20.text: Check user permissions on the backend server for every request—not just by hiding buttons on the screen.
acceptance: The server checks the signed-in user's role and permissions on every single request, not just in the browser UI.
A user cannot bypass screen buttons by calling server URLs directly.

NFR-21.text: Use HTTPS for all web traffic and encrypt sensitive ID numbers before saving them in the database.
acceptance: All traffic between the browser, server, and database is encrypted using HTTPS/TLS, and sensitive ID numbers are encrypted before being saved in the database.
Private identity numbers are never shown in plain text in logs or public responses.

NFR-22.text: Never save, log, or display plain-text passwords anywhere in the system.
acceptance: Passwords are handled and protected entirely by Supabase Auth; FindStay never stores or sees user passwords in its own database tables.
Even administrators and developers cannot view a user's password.

NFR-23.text: Check all form inputs on both the screen and server to block harmful code (SQL injection or XSS).
acceptance: All user inputs are checked for valid format and length on both the form and the server, blocking harmful code or database injection attempts.
Special characters in titles, descriptions, or reasons are displayed safely without breaking the page.

NFR-24.text: Verify record ownership before returning any property, document, or verification case by ID.
acceptance: When someone requests a property, unit, document, or verification case by its ID, the server verifies they own it or are authorised to review it.
Private verification documents use temporary signed links that expire automatically after a short time.

NFR-27.text: Block any code save that accidentally contains a password or secret key.
acceptance: Database passwords, API keys, and encryption keys are stored only in secure server environment settings—never inside the code repository.
An automatic check scans the code on every save to make sure no secret key is ever committed.

NFR-28.text: Mask Ghana Card numbers on normal screens (GHA-*******-X) so full numbers are never exposed.
acceptance: Ghana Card numbers submitted during owner verification are encrypted with AES-256 before being stored in the database.
Normal screens show only a masked version of the Ghana Card number (such as GHA-*******-X).

NFR-31.text: Keep personal contact details and verification files private and never show them on public listing pages.
acceptance: Personal contact details and verification records are kept private and never exposed on public listing responses.
The server returns only the fields needed for each screen.

NFR-32.text: Show a clear Ghana Data Protection Act, 2012 (Act 843) privacy notice during sign-up and owner verification.
acceptance: Sign-up and owner verification screens show a clear privacy notice referencing the Data Protection Commission (DPC) under Ghana's Data Protection Act, 2012 (Act 843).
The system records when each user agreed to the privacy notice and which version they accepted.

NFR-34.text: Collect the required Ghana Card, ownership proof, and tourism licence documents before approving an owner.
acceptance: Owner verification collects and checks the required regulatory documents: Ghana Card, proof of property ownership/authorisation, and Ghana Tourism Authority (GTA) licence where applicable.
Administrators can inspect each uploaded document before approving an owner.

NFR-35.text: Allow only the property owner and authorised administrators to view an owner’s personal verification records.
acceptance: Only the property owner and authorised administrators can view an owner's verification documents and personal details.
Other owners, guests, and unauthorised staff are blocked from viewing those records.

NFR-36.text: Ask only for needed personal details, and require the user to tick the privacy consent box at sign-up.
acceptance: Forms ask only for personal details that are genuinely needed to run the account and verify properties.
A user must tick the data-protection consent box before their registration is accepted.

NFR-42.text: Write a step-by-step backup restore guide and test restoring a daily backup into a test database.
acceptance: The production database is backed up automatically every day, and a written recovery guide explains how to restore it.
The team practises restoring a backup into a test database during Sprint 1 and records how long it takes.

NFR-43.text: Send server errors automatically to an error dashboard (Sentry) so the team can spot and fix bugs quickly.
acceptance: Server errors and health problems are logged automatically and reported to the monitoring dashboard so the team can fix issues quickly.
A health-check address (/actuator/health) lets the uptime monitor verify the server and database are running.

NFR-45.text: Load lists page-by-page (pagination) and add database indexes so pages stay fast as more properties join.
acceptance: Database tables and lists use indexing and page-by-page loading so the system stays fast as more owners, properties, and rooms are added.
There is no hard limit on how many properties an owner can add or how many rooms a property can have.

NFR-46.text: Store property types (Hotel, Guesthouse, Apartment, Hostel) in a database table so new types can be turned on later without changing code.
acceptance: Accommodation types (Hotel, Budget Hotel, Guesthouse, Serviced Apartment, Student Hostel) and billing periods (Nightly, Monthly, Term, Academic Year) are stored as table rows so new types can be switched on later without rebuilding the app.
Sprint 1 enables short-stay types and nightly pricing while keeping future types ready in the database.

NFR-47.text: Host the website, server, database, and photos on cloud services that can handle more traffic as FindStay grows.
acceptance: The website, backend server, database, and photo storage run on cloud services that can scale up without losing user sessions.
Photos and static files are served through a content delivery network (CDN) for fast loading across Ghana.

NFR-48.text: Split the backend server into separate folders by feature (Accounts, Companies, Verification, Listings, Calendar, Alerts, Log, Admin) so teams do not clash.
acceptance: The backend code is organised into separate, self-contained modules (Identity, Organisation, Verification, Listings, Availability, Notifications, Audit, Admin).
An automatic check fails the build if one module tries to reach into another module's private tables or code.

NFR-52.text: Save all dates and times in UTC and display them in Ghana time (GMT).
acceptance: All dates and times are saved consistently in UTC and displayed in Ghana local time (Africa/Accra, GMT+0).
Calendar blocks and activity log timestamps always match Ghana time.

NFR-54.text: Automatically generate a live list of all backend API routes so frontend and backend developers stay in sync.
acceptance: Each module has clear boundaries, clean interfaces, and an automatically generated API guide showing every available route.
The system design, database diagram, and project rules are kept in the project docs folder.

NFR-55.text: Keep a clear README and setup guide in the project folder so any team member can run the app.
acceptance: Clear written guides cover the system architecture, database tables, API endpoints, setup steps, and backup/recovery instructions.
Any new team member can follow the setup guide to run the project.

NFR-56.text: Run automatic checks on every GitHub code save and block broken code from merging.
acceptance: Every requirement in Sprint 1 has an automated test labelled with its requirement ID that runs automatically whenever code is saved.
If any automated test fails, the broken change is blocked from going live.

NFR-57.text: Keep all project code and database scripts in Git (GitHub) with version tags for each release.
acceptance: All website code, backend code, database migrations, and documentation are tracked in Git with tagged releases.
Temporary build files and secret keys are excluded from Git.

NFR-58.text: Only add new database tables or columns in updates—never delete or break existing columns.
acceptance: Sprint 1 sets up clean extension points (shared calendar blocks, listing lookup, billing periods, message templates, activity log, roles, and settings) so Sprint 2 can add bookings and payments without rewriting Sprint 1.
Every database change only adds new tables or columns—never breaking existing ones.

NFR-60.text: Connect email and SMS providers through plug-in settings so providers can be switched without rewriting code.
acceptance: Email and SMS services are connected through clean plug-in adapters so the team can switch providers by changing settings rather than rewriting features.
Message delivery is tested automatically using safe test adapters.

NFR-63.text: Use one consistent JSON format for all server responses and error messages.
acceptance: The website and backend communicate through clean, consistent JSON web addresses (/api/v1/...) with clear error messages.
An automatic check ensures new updates do not break existing web addresses.

NFR-66.text: Save the user ID, action name, affected record ID, and exact timestamp on every activity log entry.
acceptance: Every activity log entry records who performed the action, what action was taken, which record was affected, and the exact date and time.
Log entries missing any of these details are rejected by the database.

BR-02.text: Pre-load Takoradi neighbourhoods and landmarks so owners can pick their local Takoradi area.
acceptance: The location list is pre-loaded with Takoradi neighbourhoods and landmarks (such as Beach Road, Anaji, Airport Ridge, Chapel Hill, Effia-Kuma, Fijai, Tanokrom, Apollo, Market Circle, and TTU Campus).
Owners creating a listing in Release R1 can easily pick their Takoradi area and nearby landmark.

BR-03.text: Support Hotels, Budget Hotels, Guesthouses, and Serviced Apartments in Sprint 1 (with Student Hostels ready in the database for Phase 2).
acceptance: The system supports Hotels, Budget Hotels, Guesthouses, Serviced Apartments, and Student Hostels.
In Sprint 1, owners can list Hotels, Budget Hotels, Guesthouses, and Serviced Apartments, while Student Hostels are prepared in the database for Phase 2.

BR-10.text: Make the Owner Portal lightweight and easy to use on an ordinary smartphone over mobile data.
acceptance: The Owner Portal is lightweight, mobile-friendly, and easy to use on an everyday smartphone over a normal mobile data connection.
Small guesthouse and apartment owners can manage their listings and calendars without needing a computer.

BR-11.text: Log every verification check, listing approval/rejection, and account decision for accountability.
acceptance: Every listing must pass owner verification and administrator approval before going live, and every decision is permanently logged.
Administrators can suspend any listing or account that violates platform standards, with a recorded reason.

BRL-01.text: Redirect anyone who is not signed in to the Sign In page when they try to open a protected page.
acceptance: No one can access account settings, owner tools, verification uploads, listing editors, or admin screens without signing in first.
All protected routes verify the user's sign-in pass automatically.

BRL-02.text: Give each user account one primary profile and clear role assignments (Guest, Owner, Staff, Admin).
acceptance: Each user account has a primary profile and clear role memberships (Guest, Owner/Manager, Property Staff, or Administrator) per settled decision P-04.
The system always knows which role and company permissions apply to the signed-in user.

BRL-04.text: Require an owner or administrator to explicitly invite and authorise a staff member before they get access.
acceptance: A staff member gets access to a property only when an authorised owner, manager, or administrator explicitly invites them and grants permission.
No one can grant themselves staff access to a property.

BRL-05.text: Block owners and staff from viewing or editing any property that belongs to another owner’s company.
acceptance: Owners, managers, and staff can view and change only the properties and records they have been given permission to access.
The system blocks any attempt to view or change another company's properties.

BRL-06.text: Block incomplete listings from being submitted for admin approval until every required detail is filled in.
acceptance: A listing cannot be submitted for admin approval until all required details (title, description, Takoradi area, accommodation type, at least 1 unit, nightly price, at least 3 photos, amenities, and house rules) are filled in.
Incomplete listings stay saved as drafts until completed.

BRL-19.text: Record every user or listing suspension and restoration in the activity log with the written reason.
acceptance: Whenever an administrator suspends or restores a user account or property listing, they must enter a reason, and the decision is saved in the permanent activity log.
Both the suspension and restoration history remain visible in the audit log.

TA-01.text: Keep three separate folders: one for the website screens (frontend), one for the backend server, and one for the database.
acceptance: The system is divided into three clear parts: the Website screens (React), the Backend Server (Spring Boot), and the Database/Auth/Storage services (Supabase).
The website never edits business database tables directly—all business rules go through the Backend Server.

TA-02.text: Connect the website screens to the backend server using standard /api/v1/... web requests.
acceptance: The website talks to the backend server through standard, secure web requests (/api/v1/...) carrying the user's sign-in token.
Errors from the server are returned in a consistent format that the website can display clearly to the user.

TA-07.text: Let Supabase Auth store and check passwords so FindStay’s own database never stores passwords.
acceptance: Supabase Auth handles all password storage and security; FindStay's own database and server code never store or see user passwords.
Sign-up, sign-in, and password resets happen directly through Supabase Auth.

TA-08.text: Issue a 1-hour sign-in pass on login that renews automatically, and verify it on the backend server.
acceptance: When a user signs in, Supabase issues a 1-hour sign-in pass (JWT) that renews automatically while they use the app.
The backend server verifies every sign-in pass using Supabase's public verification keys and checks that the account is active on sensitive actions.

TA-09.text: Encrypt sensitive ID numbers (such as the Ghana Card number) before saving them in the database.
acceptance: Sensitive identity numbers (such as Ghana Card numbers) are encrypted before they are saved in the database.
Even if someone looks at the raw database table, the identity number is unreadable ciphertext.

TA-11.text: Store database passwords and secret API keys in cloud environment settings—never inside project files.
acceptance: All database passwords, encryption keys, and service secrets are stored in secure cloud environment settings—never written in the code files.
A template file (.env.example) lists the setting names without any real passwords.

TA-12.text: Save property photos in a public storage folder and owner verification documents in a locked private folder.
acceptance: Property photos are stored in a public photo bucket on Supabase Storage, while private verification documents are stored in a locked private bucket.
Each user can upload only to their own authorised folder.

TA-13.text: Compress uploaded property photos and convert them into fast-loading WebP images.
acceptance: Property photos are compressed and converted into fast-loading WebP images so pages load quickly on mobile networks.
Images are delivered with caching headers so repeat visits load instantly.

PD-01.text: Write the database table diagram, API list, and screen sketches before coding features.
acceptance: Before feature coding starts, the team has clear written designs for the acceptance criteria, database tables (ERD), server API routes, and screen layouts.
Every Sprint 1 story links directly to its requirements and design.

PD-02.text: Create numbered database setup scripts (V1_01 to V1_19) that build all Sprint 1 tables automatically.
acceptance: All Sprint 1 database tables, relationships, and overlap rules are created through numbered migration scripts (V1_01 to V1_19).
The database scripts run cleanly from scratch and are tested automatically.

PD-06.text: Put the website online on Cloudflare, the backend server on Render, and the database on Supabase.
acceptance: The website is hosted on Cloudflare Workers Static Assets, the backend server is hosted on Render, and the database, sign-in, and file storage run on Supabase.
All three live services are connected over HTTPS and reachable online.

PD-07.text: Set up automatic tests for individual features, database actions, and the full 7-step demo flow.
acceptance: Every story is checked at three levels: automatic unit tests, automatic database/API integration tests, and a real end-to-end walkthrough of the 7-step demo.
Every requirement ID is linked to an automated test.

PD-10.text: Add a server health-check link (/actuator/health) and an uptime alert that notifies the team if the server goes down.
acceptance: The backend server provides a live health-check address (/actuator/health) that checks both the server and database connection.
An uptime monitor checks the health address every few minutes and alerts the team if anything goes wrong.

PD-11.text: Turn on automatic daily database backups in Supabase.
acceptance: Supabase takes an automatic backup of the database every day.
During Sprint 1, the team restores a backup into a separate test database and records the time taken to prove recovery works.

PD-12.text: Store all live passwords and API keys inside GitHub, Render, and Cloudflare secret settings.
acceptance: All live passwords and API keys are stored in Cloudflare, Render, and GitHub secret settings—never in source code.
Automatic checks verify that no secrets are ever pushed to GitHub.
